name: Beignets
desc: New Orleans style yeast-raised dough squares, deep fried until puffed and buried in powdered sugar.

source.title: French Market Beignets
source.evidence: Matches the site's 1/2 cup sugar, 1 cup evaporated milk, 7 cups flour and 1/4 cup shortening; supplies the water, yeast, salt and eggs the site lacked.

ingredients.raw: 1 cup evaporated milk (from a 12 oz can)
7 cups all-purpose flour, divided, plus more for rolling
1-2 quarts vegetable or peanut oil, for deep frying (enough for 2 inches in the pot)
ingredients.note: enough for 2 inches in the pot

steps: Pour the warm water into a large bowl, sprinkle the yeast over it, and stir to dissolve. Let stand about 5 minutes, until foamy.
Stir in the sugar, salt, eggs and evaporated milk. Add 4 cups of the flour and beat until smooth.
Mix in the shortening, then the remaining 3 cups flour, to a soft dough.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate at least 2 hours, or up to 24 hours.
On a floured surface, roll the dough 1/8 inch thick and cut into 2 1/2-inch squares. Cover loosely and let rise until slightly puffy, about 30 minutes.

Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 360°F. Fry a few squares at a time, turning once, about 3 minutes total, until puffed and light golden brown. If they sink and do not float up, the oil is not hot enough.
Drain on paper towels and shake powdered sugar over the hot beignets. Serve right away.
tips: The food.com version cuts a double slash through the center of each square to help the middle cook through.
Any dough you are not frying keeps in the fridge up to 24 hours from when it was mixed.

references.title: Beignets
references.usedFor: adding flour in two stages, 2 to 24 hour chill, oil temperature test

references.title: French Market Beignets
